marriedInOregon.description: If the marriage was solemnized in Oregon, at least one party must be a resident of Oregon at the time of filing. No minimum duration is required.

marriedOutsideOregon.description: If the marriage was not solemnized in Oregon, at least one party must have been a resident of Oregon continuously for at least 6 months immediately preceding the filing.

waitingPeriod.description: Oregon has NO mandatory waiting period. The 90-day waiting period was repealed in 2011. A dissolution can be finalized as soon as the court is ready to enter judgment.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences that have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

groundsForDissolution.notes: Oregon is a purely no-fault state. The only ground for dissolution is irreconcilable differences that have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage. ORS §107.025.

propertyDivision.description: Oregon divides marital property in a manner that is 'just and proper in all the circumstances.' There is a rebuttable presumption that both spouses contributed equally to the acquisition of property during the marriage, regardless of which spouse actually earned the income.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before marriage or by gift or inheritance during the marriage may be treated as separate property, but the court has broad discretion to divide all property.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirements — conditional on where marriage was solemnized
Grounds for dissolution — irreconcilable differences only (no-fault)
Property division — equitable distribution with rebuttable presumption of equal contribution
Spousal support — transitional, compensatory, and spousal maintenance
Joint custody — requires agreement of both parents
Parenting plan — required for cases involving minor children
Oregon Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: Oregon filing fees are approximately $301 for a dissolution of marriage petition. Fee waivers or deferrals are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Petition for Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Initiates the dissolution proceeding (or Co-Petition if filed jointly)

basic.name: Summons
basic.description: Formal notice to respondent (not required for co-petitions)

basic.name: Certificate of Readiness
basic.description: Filed when the case is ready for judgment

basic.name: Judgment of Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage (Oregon calls this a 'Judgment')

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on respondent via sheriff, process server, or certified mail

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Required plan detailing minimum parenting time for each parent (ORS §107.102)

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheets
withChildren.description: Calculation per Oregon Child Support Guidelines (ORS §25.275)

withChildren.name: Uniform Support Declaration
withChildren.description: Income and expense declaration for child support calculation

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Oregon Uniform Trial Court Rules (UTCR)

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Oregon must file a response within 30 days of service (additional time may apply per ORCP 7)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Oregon uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Oregon Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined adjusted income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate. Parenting time adjustments may apply.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Oregon provides three types of spousal support: (1) Transitional support — to help a spouse become self-supporting through education, training, or work experience; (2) Compensatory support — to compensate a spouse who contributed to the other's education, training, or earning capacity; (3) Spousal maintenance — ongoing support for a spouse who cannot meet basic needs through full-time employment at a standard of living not overly disproportionate to that enjoyed during the marriage.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: The court considers the duration of the marriage, the age and health of the parties, the standard of living during the marriage, the relative income and earning capacity of each party, and the extent to which one spouse contributed to the education or career of the other.

court.name: Circuit Court
court.description: Dissolution of marriage is filed in the Circuit Court in the county where either party resides.
